t: Species taxonomy, phylogeny and biogeography of the Brontotheriidae (Mammalia, Perissodactyla) ; Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History, no. 311
s: The present study reevaluates the species taxonomy of brontotheres based on craniodental materials. All known taxa were considered for revision except North American representatives of Eotitanops, Palaeosyops, and Megacerops. A phylogenetic species concept, where species are defined as the smallest diagnosable clusters of specimens, was adopted for this study.

t: About the Animals: Brontotheres | Nebraska Public Media
s: In North America, Brontothere species evolved to have larger bodies with pairs of horny appendages on their skulls, useful for fighting and protecting young. Fossils of the two main species that evolved have been found in northern Colorado, western Nebraska, eastern Wyoming, the South Dakota badlands, and as far north as Saskatchewan.
